smt-2022-algebra-01.title: Rationalise each term
smt-2022-algebra-01.body:
The $k$-th term ($k=2,\dots,31$) is $\dfrac{2k+1+\sqrt{k(k+1)}}{\sqrt k+\sqrt{k+1}}$. Multiply top and bottom by $\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k$; the denominator becomes $1$. With $a=\sqrt{k+1}$, $b=\sqrt k$ the numerator is $a^2+b^2+ab$ (since $2k+1=a^2+b^2$, $\sqrt{k(k+1)}=ab$), so the term equals $(a^2+ab+b^2)(a-b)=a^3-b^3=(k+1)^{3/2}-k^{3/2}$.

The sum telescopes: $32^{3/2}-2^{3/2}=128\sqrt2-2\sqrt2=126\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $126\sqrt2$**

smt-2022-algebra-02.title: Reduce to a quadratic
smt-2022-algebra-02.body:
A solution satisfies $x\ge0$. Let $y=\sqrt{2022+x}$, so $x=\sqrt{2022+y}$. Then $y^2-x=2022$ and $x^2-y=2022$; subtracting gives $(y-x)(y+x+1)=0$. Since $x,y\ge0$, $x+y+1>0$ so $y=x$, hence $x=\sqrt{2022+x}$, i.e. $x^2-x-2022=0$.

The roots are $\frac{1\pm\sqrt{8089}}{2}$; only the positive one is valid. So the only solution, and thus the sum, is $\frac{1+\sqrt{8089}}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{1+\sqrt{8089}}{2}$**

smt-2022-algebra-03.title: Bound the harmonic sum
smt-2022-algebra-03.body:
There are $43$ terms. Each is at most $\frac1{2022}$ and at least $\frac1{2064}$, so $\frac{43}{2064}<S<\frac{43}{2022}$ where $S$ is the sum.

Therefore $\frac{2022}{43}<\frac1S<\frac{2064}{43}=48$. Since $\frac{2022}{43}=47\frac{1}{43}>47$, we get $47<\frac1S<48$.

**Answer: 47**

smt-2022-algebra-04.title: Factor the double sums
smt-2022-algebra-04.body:
$\sum_{i,j}r_is_j=\left(\sum r_i\right)\left(\sum s_j\right)$. By Vieta, the sums of roots are $7$, $8$, $9$ respectively (the $x^{2021}$ coefficient with the sign changed).

So the total is $7\cdot8+8\cdot9+9\cdot7=56+72+63=191$.

**Answer: 191**

smt-2022-algebra-05.title: AM-GM
smt-2022-algebra-05.body:
$x^3y^3z^3=1000$, so we must minimise $3x^4+12y^2+12z^4$. Write it as $3x^4+6y^2+6y^2+12z^4$ and apply AM-GM to these four terms:

$$3x^4+6y^2+6y^2+12z^4\ge4\sqrt[4]{3\cdot6\cdot6\cdot12\,x^4y^4z^4}=4\sqrt[4]{1296}\,|xyz|=24\cdot10=240.$$

Equality needs $3x^4=6y^2=12z^4=t$; then $|xyz|=t/6$, so $t=60$ gives $xyz=10$ (choose signs so $xyz>0$), and the bound is attained.

Thus the maximum is $1000-240=760$.

**Answer: 760**

smt-2022-algebra-06.title: Telescoping arccotangents
smt-2022-algebra-06.body:
$1+\sum_{k=1}^n2k=1+n(n+1)$. Using $\cot^{-1}a-\cot^{-1}b=\cot^{-1}\frac{ab+1}{b-a}$ with $a=n$, $b=n+1$ gives $\cot^{-1}n-\cot^{-1}(n+1)=\cot^{-1}(n(n+1)+1)$.

So the sum is $\sum_{n=1}^{23}\left(\cot^{-1}n-\cot^{-1}(n+1)\right)=\cot^{-1}1-\cot^{-1}24=\cot^{-1}\frac{1\cdot24+1}{24-1}=\cot^{-1}\frac{25}{23}$.

Hence the cotangent is $\frac{25}{23}$.

**Answer: $\frac{25}{23}$**

smt-2022-algebra-07.title: No such function exists
smt-2022-algebra-07.body:
Suppose $f$ exists. If $f(b,a)=c$ then $f(a,c)=b$, and then $f(c,b)=f(c,f(a,c))=a$. So the triple $(x,y,z)$ with $f(x,y)=z$ belongs to the set $S$ exactly when its cyclic shift $(y,z,x)$ does.

The cyclic shift partitions $S$ into orbits of size $3$ or $1$; size $1$ means $x=y=z$, i.e. $f(x,x)=x$, which is forbidden. So $3\mid|S|$. But $|S|=|M|^2=2023^2$ (one triple for each pair $(x,y)$), and $2023=3\cdot674+1$ is not divisible by $3$. Contradiction.

So there are $0$ such functions, and $0\bmod1000=0$.

**Answer: 0**

smt-2022-algebra-08.title: Count the possible solutions
smt-2022-algebra-08.body:
Let $N=mx=\lfloor x^{11/10}\rfloor$, an integer, so $x=N/m$. The condition is $N\le(N/m)^{11/10}<N+1$.

The left inequality is equivalent to $N^{1/10}\ge m^{11/10}$, i.e. $N\ge m^{11}$. Write $N=m^{11}+j$ with $j\ge0$ an integer. Then
$$\left(\frac Nm\right)^{11/10}=N\left(\frac{N}{m^{11}}\right)^{1/10}=N\left(1+\frac{j}{m^{11}}\right)^{1/10}\approx N+\frac{j}{10}\cdot\frac{N}{m^{11}}\approx N+\frac j{10},$$

where the errors are negligible because $m$ is huge. So the right inequality holds exactly when $j/10<1$, i.e. $j=0,1,\dots,9$.

This gives at most $10$ solutions, and the same computation shows all ten occur for $m=10^{2022}+1$. The maximum is $10$.

**Answer: 10**

smt-2022-algebra-09.title: Force the cubic to be a perfect cube
smt-2022-algebra-09.body:
If $r=0$ then $x_0=p+\sqrt q$ would be a root of a cubic with rational coefficients lying in a field of degree at most $2$, which forces a rational root; so $r\ne0$. Similarly one shows (official solution) that $x_0$ cannot lie in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)$ unless $P$ has a rational root, and this forces $P(x)=8\left((x-p-\sqrt q)^3-r\right)$ with $q=0$ (the coefficients of $P$ are rational).

So $P(x)=8(x-p)^3-8r=8x^3-24p\,x^2+24p^2x-(8p^3+8r)$ with $8p^3+8r=-1$. Therefore $a=-24p$, $b=24p^2$ and $a+b=24(p^2-p)=24\left[(p-\tfrac12)^2-\tfrac14\right]\ge-6$, with equality at $p=\frac12$.

Then $r=-\frac14$ and $P(x)=8x^3-12x^2+6x+1=(2x-1)^3+2$, which has no rational root and works. So the minimum is $-6$.

**Answer: $-6$**

smt-2022-algebra-10.title: Track the two lowest coefficients
smt-2022-algebra-10.body:
Write $f^{n}(x)=c_nx+d_nx^3+\cdots$ (an odd polynomial). Then $f^{n}(x)=f^{n-1}(x^3-3x)$ gives, using $g=f^{n-1}=c_{n-1}x+d_{n-1}x^3+\cdots$: $g(x^3-3x)=c_{n-1}(x^3-3x)+d_{n-1}(-3x)^3+\cdots$, so $c_n=-3c_{n-1}$ and $d_n=c_{n-1}-27d_{n-1}$. Start: $c_1=-3$, $d_1=1$.

Let $\rho_n=d_n/c_n$. Then $\rho_n=\frac{c_{n-1}-27d_{n-1}}{-3c_{n-1}}=-\frac13+9\rho_{n-1}$, $\rho_1=-\frac13$. This is solved by $\rho_n=-\frac{3^{2n}-1}{24}$ (check: $-\frac13+9\cdot\left(-\frac{3^{2n-2}-1}{24}\right)=-\frac{8+3^{2n}-9}{24}$).

The polynomial $f^n(x)/x=c_n+d_nx^2+\cdots$ has $3^n-1$ roots, all nonzero (it is a polynomial in $u=x^2$ with nonzero constant term $c_n$). Its roots in $u$ satisfy $\sum 1/u_i=-d_n/c_n$ by Vieta, and each $u$ comes from two roots $\pm x$, so $$\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\frac1{r^2}=-2\rho_n=\frac{3^{2n}-1}{12}.$$ (Check $n=1$: roots $\pm\sqrt3$, sum $\frac23=\frac{9-1}{12}$.)

For $n=2022$ this is $\frac{3^{4044}-1}{12}$, so $a=3$, $b=4044$, $c=1$, $d=12$, and $a+b+c+d=4060$.

**Answer: 4060**
